subject: Mathematics
title: Priya's Toy Giveaway
hook: How do you give away toys when you don't have enough ones?

slides.title: Priya's Toy Giveaway
slides.inSimpleWords: Learn how to subtract when ones aren't enough!

slides.title: The Toy Problem
slides.storyContext: Priya has 32 toys and wants to give away 15 toys to her cousin. But there's a catch: She has only 2 ones and needs to give away 5!

points.label: The challenge
points.text: 32 - 15. But 2 is smaller than 5!

slides.inSimpleWords: Sometimes we need to borrow from tens!

image.alt: The Toy Problem — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: What is Subtraction?
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'What does 32 - 15 mean?' Priya explains: 'It means starting with 32 and taking away 15!'

points.label: Definition
points.text: Subtraction = taking away or removing a smaller number from a larger number. The symbol is - (minus).

slides.title: Set Up the Problem
slides.storyContext: Ravi writes it down: 32 on top, 15 below it. 'Ones under ones, tens under tens!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Ones line up with ones, tens with tens.

image.alt: Set Up the Problem — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: Tens and Ones Review
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'Remember! 32 has 3 tens (thirty) and 2 ones (two). So 32 = 30 + 2. And 15 has 1 ten (ten) and 5 ones (five).'

points.label: Breaking it down
points.text: 32 = 3 tens + 2 ones. 15 = 1 ten + 5 ones.

slides.inSimpleWords: Every number has tens and ones!

slides.title: The Problem in Ones
slides.storyContext: Priya tries: 2 - 5 = ? 'Wait! I can't take 5 from 2. I need more ones!'

example.solution: We can't! So we need to borrow from the tens.

slides.inSimpleWords: 2 is too small to subtract 5 from.

image.alt: The Problem in Ones — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: What Happens When We Can't Subtract?
slides.storyContext: Ravi says, 'In the ones place, we have 2. We need to take away 5. We can't do 2 - 5 = ? The small number can't give to the big number!'

example.solution: No. We need more ones. That's where borrowing comes in!

slides.inSimpleWords: When the top ones are smaller, we borrow!

slides.title: What is Borrowing?
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'Borrowing means we take 1 ten and turn it into 10 ones. It's like trading!' Ravi nods: 'So we use the extra ones to subtract!'

points.label: The idea
points.text: Borrowing = trading 1 ten for 10 ones. This gives us more ones to subtract.

slides.inSimpleWords: Borrowing is trading 1 ten for 10 ones!

slides.title: Borrow a Ten
slides.storyContext: Ravi says, 'One of your 3 tens can become 10 ones! Take 1 ten from the tens.' Priya has 2 tens left and 12 ones now!

points.label: Borrowing
points.text: Break 1 ten into 10 ones. So 3 tens become 2 tens, and 2 ones become 12 ones.

image.alt: Borrow a Ten — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: Try Borrowing
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: 'If we start with 3 tens and 2 ones, and we borrow 1 ten, how many tens and ones do we have now?' Ravi counts: '2 tens and 12 ones!'

points.label: Practice
points.text: Before borrowing: 3 tens, 2 ones. After borrowing: 2 tens, 12 ones.

slides.title: Subtract the Ones
slides.storyContext: Now Priya has 12 ones. 'Twelve minus five is... 7!' She writes 7 in the ones place.

image.alt: Subtract the Ones — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: Subtract the Tens
slides.storyContext: After borrowing, Priya has 2 tens left. 'Two tens minus 1 ten equals 1 ten.' She writes 1 in the tens place.

image.alt: Subtract the Tens — Subtraction with Borrowing

slides.title: The Answer
slides.storyContext: Ravi checks: 1 ten and 7 ones = 17. 'So 32 - 15 = 17 toys left!'

slides.title: Another Example: 41 - 26
slides.storyContext: Ravi tries a new one. 1 - 6 won't work, so borrow 1 ten. Now 11 - 6 = 5. Then 3 - 2 = 1. Answer: 15!

slides.title: Why Borrow?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'When ones are too small, we break a ten into 10 ones. It's like exchanging a big coin for 10 small ones!'

points.label: Understanding
points.text: Borrowing = trading 1 ten for 10 ones.

slides.title: Example: 50 - 23
slides.storyContext: Ravi writes 50 - 23. 'In the ones: 0 - 3 won't work! So I borrow 1 ten. Now I have 10 - 3 = 7. And 4 - 2 = 2 (in tens). Answer: 27!'

slides.title: Try: 53 - 28
slides.storyContext: Ravi writes: 3 - 8 won't work. Borrow 1 ten! 13 - 8 = 5. Then 4 - 2 = 2. Answer: 25!

points.label: Practice
points.text: 53 - 28 = 25. Borrow from tens, subtract ones, subtract tens.

slides.title: Steps for Subtraction with Borrowing
slides.storyContext: Priya lists the steps: '1. Write the numbers. 2. Look at ones. 3. If top ones < bottom ones, borrow! 4. Subtract ones. 5. Subtract tens. 6. Write the answer!'

points.label: Algorithm
points.text: Step 1: Set up (bigger number on top). Step 2: Check ones (can we subtract?). Step 3: If no, borrow 1 ten. Step 4: Subtract ones first. Step 5: Subtract tens. Step 6: Read the answer.

slides.title: Example: 32 - 15 Full Walkthrough
slides.storyContext: Ravi teaches step by step: '32 on top, 15 below. Ones: 2 - 5? No! Borrow → 12 - 5 = 7. Tens: 2 - 1 = 1. Answer: 17!'

example.solution: Setup: 32 on top. Check ones: 2 < 5, so borrow. New: 12 - 5 = 7 (ones). Tens: 2 - 1 = 1. Answer: 17.

slides.title: Challenge: 60 - 34
slides.storyContext: Priya asks, 'Ravi, what about 60 - 34?' Ravi: 'Ones: 0 - 4, borrow! 10 - 4 = 6. Tens: 5 - 3 = 2. Answer: 26!'

points.label: Challenge
points.text: 60 - 34 = 26. Remember to borrow even when ones are 0!

slides.inSimpleWords: Borrowing works even when ones are 0!

slides.title: Common Mistakes
slides.storyContext: Priya warns: 'Don't forget to cross out the old tens digit when you borrow! Write the new digit above it. And borrow BEFORE you subtract!'

example.problem: What if we forget to borrow?
example.solution: Then 2 - 5 = wrong! Always check: if top ones < bottom ones, borrow first.

slides.title: Verification: Check Your Work
slides.storyContext: Ravi says, 'To check if 32 - 15 = 17 is right, add: 17 + 15 should equal 32!' Priya nods: '17 + 15 = 32. Correct!'

points.label: Check
points.text: Answer + subtracted number = original number. So 17 + 15 = 32 ✓

slides.inSimpleWords: Verify by adding the answer back!

slides.title: Example: 71 - 35
slides.storyContext: Ravi practices: '71 - 35. Ones: 1 - 5 won't work. Borrow! 11 - 5 = 6. Tens: 6 - 3 = 3. Answer: 36!'

slides.title: Challenge: 82 - 47
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: '82 - 47?' Ravi: 'Ones: 2 - 7, borrow! 12 - 7 = 5. Tens: 7 - 4 = 3. Answer: 35!'

points.label: Practice
points.text: 82 - 47 = 35. Master the borrowing step!

slides.title: Real Problem: Toys Left
slides.storyContext: Priya started with 32 toys. She gave away 15. Using borrowing, she now knows she has 17 left. 'All my toys are counted!'

points.label: Story ends
points.text: 32 toys - 15 given away = 17 toys remaining. Borrowing solved the problem!

slides.inSimpleWords: Borrowing helps us with real problems!

slides.title: Priya's Gift Complete
slides.storyContext: Priya counts 17 toys remaining. 'Borrowing helped me solve the problem. When ones aren't enough, we borrow from tens!'

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Check if ones can be subtracted. 2. If not, borrow 1 ten (becomes 10 ones). 3. Subtract ones. 4. Subtract tens (remember you borrowed!). 5. Write the answer.

slides.inSimpleWords: Borrowing is trading 1 ten for 10 ones!

image.alt: Priya's Gift Complete — Subtraction with Borrowing

subject: Mathematics
title: Ravi's Bakery Helper Adventure
hook: Can Ravi arrange cookies in perfect groups for the bakery?

slides.title: Cookies by the Box
slides.storyContext: Priya is packing cookies. 'Ravi, put 2 cookies in each box. If I have 5 boxes, how many cookies do we need?'

points.label: The task
points.text: Count groups: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = ?

image.alt: Cookies by the Box — Multiplication Tables 2-5

slides.title: What is Multiplication?
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'Multiplication is a fast way to count groups. Instead of adding 2+2+2+2+2, we can say 5 times 2, or 5 × 2!'

points.label: Definition
points.text: Multiplication = repeated addition. The symbol is × (times).

slides.title: Groups Make Multiplication
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees 3 boxes, each with 2 cookies. 'That's 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. Or... 3 times 2 = 3 × 2 = 6!'

example.problem: 3 boxes with 2 cookies each. How many cookies?

slides.title: Parts of a Multiplication Problem
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'In 5 × 2, the 5 means how many groups, and 2 means how many in each group. So 5 groups of 2!'

points.label: Reading multiplication
points.text: 5 × 2 = 5 groups of 2. First number = number of groups. Second number = items per group.

slides.title: Table of 2
slides.storyContext: Ravi lines up cookies: 2, then 4, then 6, then 8, then 10! 'I see a pattern, Priya! It goes up by 2 each time!'

slides.title: 2 Times Tables (Repetition)
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 1×2=2, 2×2=4, 3×2=6, 4×2=8, 5×2=10. 'See? Ravi, each number gets the pattern!'

slides.title: Practice Table of 2
slides.storyContext: Ravi recites: '1×2=2, 2×2=4, 3×2=6, 4×2=8, 5×2=10!' Priya claps: 'Perfect! Now you know table of 2!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Table of 2 is easy once you know it!

slides.title: Table of 5
slides.storyContext: Now Priya uses fingers to count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50! 'Look at your hands, Ravi! Each hand has 5 fingers!'

slides.title: 5 Times Tables
slides.storyContext: Ravi uses fingers: 1×5=5 (one hand), 2×5=10 (two hands), 3×5=15, and so on!

slides.title: Pattern in Table of 5
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'Look at the last digit in table of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25... They always end in 5 or 0!'

slides.title: Practice Table of 5
slides.storyContext: Ravi practices: '1×5=5, 2×5=10, 3×5=15, 4×5=20, 5×5=25!' Priya smiles: 'All fives end in 0 or 5!'

slides.title: Table of 3 and 4
slides.inSimpleWords: Tables of 3 and 4 have their own patterns!

slides.title: Table of 3
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts: '1×3=3, 2×3=6, 3×3=9, 4×3=12, 5×3=15. The numbers keep jumping by 3!'

slides.title: Table of 4
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: '1×4=4, 2×4=8, 3×4=12, 4×4=16, 5×4=20. Table of 4 jumps by 4 each time!'

slides.title: Multiplication Story
slides.storyContext: Priya asks, 'Ravi, if I have 4 cookie boxes with 5 cookies in each, how many cookies total?'

points.label: Real problem
points.text: 4 × 5 = 20 cookies

slides.title: Comparing Tables
slides.storyContext: Ravi notices: '2×5=10, but 5×2 also=10!' Priya smiles. 'The order doesn't matter in multiplication, Ravi!'

example.solution: Yes! Both equal 10. Multiplication works both ways.

slides.title: Why Commutative Property?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'If you have 3 rows of 4 cookies, that's 12. If you turn it sideways, 4 rows of 3 cookies, still 12!'

points.label: Understanding
points.text: 3 × 4 = 4 × 3 because rearranging groups doesn't change the total.

slides.inSimpleWords: Switching groups gives the same answer!

slides.title: Quick Recall
slides.storyContext: Priya writes all tables on the wall. 'Ravi, let's practice saying them fast: 2×3=6, 3×4=12, 5×5=25! Soon you'll know them by heart!'

points.label: Memorizing
points.text: Repeat tables: 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s. Repetition helps!

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice tables until they become automatic!

slides.title: All Tables Summary
slides.storyContext: Ravi summarizes: 'Table of 2: goes by 2s. Table of 3: goes by 3s. Table of 4: goes by 4s. Table of 5: ends in 5 or 0!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Each table has its own pattern!

slides.title: The Market
slides.storyContext: At the market, Ravi sees: 'Apples are ₹3 each. If I buy 5 apples, how much is it?' 5×3=15, so ₹15!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Multiplication helps with money and shopping!

slides.title: Problem: Arrange Cookies in Boxes
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'We need to ship 3 boxes with 4 cookies in each. How many cookies total?' Ravi: '3 × 4 = 12 cookies!'

slides.title: Mixed Multiplications
slides.storyContext: Priya quizzes: '2×5? 4×3? 5×4? 3×2?' Ravi answers: '10! 12! 20! 6! I'm a times table master!'

slides.title: Problem: Bakery Order
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts: 'Priya needs 4 trays with 5 cookies each. That's 4 × 5 = 20 cookies to bake!'

slides.title: Multiplication vs Addition
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'Adding: 5+5+5+5 takes longer. Multiplying: 4×5 is faster!' Ravi nods: 'Multiplication is a shortcut for repeated adding!'

points.label: Why multiply?
points.text: Multiplication is faster than adding the same number many times.

slides.title: Tables Learned!
slides.storyContext: Priya and Ravi sit tired but happy. 'We learned that multiplication is groups and repeated adding. Tables 2, 3, 4, 5 are our new friends!'

points.label: Final
points.text: 1. Multiplication = groups. 2. Table of 2: 2,4,6,8,10... 3. Table of 5: 5,10,15,20,25... 4. Table of 3 and 4 have patterns too. 5. Use for shopping and real problems!

slides.inSimpleWords: Multiplication tables help us count groups fast!

subject: Mathematics
title: Priya's Festival Market
hook: Can Ravi count enough rupees to buy all the festival treats?

slides.title: Priya's Festival Market
slides.inSimpleWords: Learn to count money and make purchases!

slides.title: Festival Day Shopping
slides.storyContext: It's festival day! Ravi has coins and notes in his pocket. 'Priya, help me count my money! I want to buy sweets!'

points.label: Task
points.text: Count coins: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10. Count notes: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50.

slides.inSimpleWords: Indian money has coins and colorful notes!

slides.title: What is Money?
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'Money is something we use to buy things. In India, we use rupees. The symbol is ₹!'

points.label: Definition
points.text: Money = a way to pay for things. Indian money = Rupees (₹).

slides.inSimpleWords: Money helps us buy what we need!

slides.title: Indian Coins
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi: 'Look! Small ₹1 coin, then ₹2, then ₹5, then big ₹10 coin. Each is worth different amounts!'

points.label: Coins
points.text: ₹1 coin (small), ₹2 coin, ₹5 coin, ₹10 coin (big)

slides.title: Comparing Coin Values
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks: 'Is ₹5 coin worth more than ₹2 coin?' Priya nods: 'Yes! ₹5 is worth 2.5 times more!'

example.solution: ₹10 coin! It's worth ten times more than ₹1.

slides.title: Indian Notes
slides.storyContext: Priya pulls out paper money: 'Here's a red ₹10 note, then a blue-green ₹20 note, then a pink ₹50 note! Each worth more!'

points.label: Notes
points.text: ₹10 (red), ₹20 (blue-green), ₹50 (pink), ₹100 (green)

slides.inSimpleWords: Notes are colorful and worth more money!

slides.title: Comparing Note Values
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks: 'Is ₹20 worth more than ₹10?' Priya: 'Yes! ₹20 is twice ₹10. So one ₹20 note = two ₹10 notes!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Notes can be made from smaller notes!

slides.title: Counting Coins
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts: 'I have 3 rupees in ₹1 coins, plus 1 rupee in a ₹5 coin... wait! That's just 1 rupee, not 5 rupees!'

slides.title: Counting Notes
slides.storyContext: Priya counts: 'One ₹50 note, one ₹20 note, one ₹10 note. That's 50 + 20 + 10 = 80 rupees!'

example.problem: Count: one ₹50 note + one ₹20 note + one ₹10 note.

slides.title: Mixed Money
slides.storyContext: Ravi now counts everything: '2 rupees in coins plus 80 rupees in notes. That's ₹82 total! Will it buy my sweets?'

points.label: All together
points.text: ₹8 (coins) + ₹80 (notes) = ₹88

slides.title: Shopping at the Stall
slides.storyContext: The sweet seller says, 'Laddu is ₹10 each. Jalebi is ₹15 a plate. Kheer costs ₹20.' Ravi thinks hard!

example.problem: Ravi has ₹30. Can he buy 1 Jalebi (₹15) and 1 Kheer (₹20)?
example.solution: ₹15 + ₹20 = ₹35. No, he needs ₹5 more. He has only ₹30.

image.alt: Shopping at the Stall — Money Counting

slides.title: Making Change
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'If your ₹50 note pays for ₹30 worth of sweets, the seller gives you ₹20 change. 50 - 30 = 20!'

points.label: Change
points.text: Money given - Money spent = Change left

slides.inSimpleWords: Change is money you get back!

slides.title: Calculating Change
slides.storyContext: Ravi pays with ₹100 for ₹70 worth of sweets. 'How much change do I get?' Priya: '100 - 70 = 30 rupees!'

slides.title: Real Purchase
slides.storyContext: Ravi buys 2 laddus (₹10 each) and 1 jalebi (₹15). He pays with ₹50. How much change?

slides.title: Different Coins Make Same Value
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'Five ₹2 coins = 1 ₹10 coin. Same value, different coins!' Ravi's eyes light up.

example.problem: Are five ₹2 coins worth the same as one ₹10 coin?

slides.inSimpleWords: Different coins can make the same amount!

image.alt: Different Coins Make Same Value — Money Counting

slides.title: Budgeting: Plan Your Money
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'If you have ₹100, you can make a list: Sweets ₹40, Toys ₹30, Save ₹30. Plan before you spend!'

points.label: Smart spending
points.text: List items and prices. Add them up. Check if you have enough.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plan your spending before you buy!

slides.title: Budget Challenge
slides.storyContext: Ravi has ₹100. Wants: cookies ₹25, juice ₹20, toy ₹40. Can he buy all? '25+20+40 = 85. Yes! With ₹15 left!'

slides.title: Money Combinations
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'To make ₹50, you could use: one ₹50 note, OR five ₹10 notes, OR two ₹20 notes and one ₹10 note!'

example.solution: Three ₹10 notes, OR one ₹20 note + one ₹10 note.

slides.inSimpleWords: Money can be made many ways!

slides.title: Shopping Mall Adventure
slides.storyContext: Ravi has ₹200. Book (₹50), Pen (₹20), Notebook (₹15), Snack (₹30). Total? '50+20+15+30=115. I have ₹85 left!'

points.label: Real scenario
points.text: Total spent: ₹115. Change: ₹200 - ₹115 = ₹85.

slides.title: Skip Counting by 5s (Money Trick)
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches a trick: 'If counting ₹5 coins: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25! It's just like table of 5!' Ravi smiles: 'Multiplication helps money counting!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Use multiplication to count money faster!

slides.title: Multiple Coins Practice
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts: '2 coins of ₹5 = 10, plus 3 coins of ₹2 = 6, plus 4 coins of ₹1 = 4. Total: 10 + 6 + 4 = 20 rupees!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Add all coins and notes together!

slides.title: Quick Counting with Multiplication
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'If you have 6 coins of ₹10, don't count 10+10+10+10+10+10. Just do 6×10=60!' Ravi smiles: 'Multiplication helps count money faster!'

points.label: Speed tip
points.text: Use multiplication when you have many of the same coin or note.

slides.title: Exact Change Problem
slides.storyContext: At the market, Ravi buys items for ₹47. He gives ₹50. The seller says, 'Here's ₹3 change.' Ravi checks: '50 - 47 = 3. Yes! That's correct!'

points.label: Check change
points.text: Amount given (₹50) - Cost (₹47) = Change (₹3).

slides.title: Saving Money
slides.storyContext: Ravi saves ₹20 per week. After 4 weeks, he has 4×20 = ₹80! 'Now I can buy that toy!' Priya nods: 'Saving adds up!'

example.problem: Save ₹20 per week for 4 weeks. Total?

slides.title: Money in Real Life
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'Money helps us buy food, clothes, toys, and books. We earn it by working and use it wisely by planning our spending.'

points.label: Using money
points.text: Money is earned, saved, and spent wisely for things we need and want.

slides.inSimpleWords: Money helps us live and have fun!

slides.title: Money Mastered!
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats his sweets happily. 'Priya, I know coins and notes now! Counting money is like counting numbers!'

points.label: Learning
points.text: 1. Indian coins: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10. 2. Indian notes: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100. 3. Add coins and notes together. 4. Check prices. 5. Calculate change. 6. Money math is number math!
